newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELKINGTON WINS DORAL-RYDER OPEN BY TWO STROKES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELKINGTON WINS DORAL-RYDER OPEN BY TWO STROKES.

text.p: An eagle from the fairway on the par four third hole -- the second most difficult on the Blue Monster course -- set up Australian Steve Elkington for a two-stroke victory at the Doral-Ryder Open on Sunday.
The eagle brought Elkington to 13-under-par and set the tone for his final round 69 and 13-under 275 winning total.
"After the six-iron went in on number three, I felt that this was going to be my day, I'm going to make it my day," Elkington recalled.
"There was no reason to back off at that point," added Elkington after his seventh career win but first since the 1995 PGA Championship.

Nick Price of Zimbabwe shot an even-par 72 to finish tied for second place at 11-under 277, along with 49-year-old Larry Nelson, who shot 70. Overnight leader David Duval stumbled to a final-round 74 and finished fourth.
In addition to his eagle, Elkington also had two bogeys -- both caused by bunkers on the 13th and 14th holes -- and birdies on the first, ninth and 10th holes.
"I was protecting from the 10th hole onwards. The holes are so hard coming in, it's not realistic to try to set up birdies," Elkington said of the notorious Blue Monster layout.
"I was hitting my irons as well as anyone out there, and so if it was tough for me to get it close, I knew no one else was going to either," he said.
"Greg Norman always says that the reason he plays so well here is that he knows where to hit the ball, and it's the same for me, I know how to play Doral," Elkington said.
Three-time Doral winner Norman, however, closed with consecutive 74s to finish seven strokes off the pace.

"After shooting 66 on Friday, I told my caddy that I thought I could win this -- even though I haven't really played much at all this year, and don't feel that comfy -- because my putting was so solid," said Elkington, who earned $324,000 when his prediction came true.
Price birdied the first hole, bogeyed the sixth, and parred the rest of the course to just miss a third consecutive win after taking back-to-back titles in South Africa.
"It was hard to get the ball close today. I kept hitting the ball 30 feet from the hole and I didn't make any," said Price, who has not won in North America since the 1994 Canadian Open.
"I made only two long putts all day, and they were both to save par," Price said.
"All in all it was a really good week for me, because I've never played that well on this golf course, so to shoot 11 under par is refreshing," he added.
The most consistent performance of the week came from Nelson, who is due to join the Senior Tour in September.
On a difficult course where 92 double bogeys were recorded, and 10 scores even higher, Nelson suffered a tournament-low six bogeys over 72 holes.
"I proved a lot to myself, whether I proved anything to anyone else doesn't matter," he said.
